build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

comments.text: GDRIVE01, the 3D view's driver: 25 JMPs the modules call at fixed addresses. $C000 view_init, $C003 draw_view, $C006-$C015 the processor-port switches, $C018 square_info, $C01B clear_view, $C01E step_forward, $C021 and $C024 block copies, $C027 show_view, $C02A square_index, $C02D-$C036 the map's object records, $C039 and $C03C draw_objects, $C03F load_object_sprites; the last three, $C042-$C048, jump to $C90F, where there is no routine, and nothing calls them.
draw_view's jump; gdrive_call ($4078) calls it with BASIC's ROM bit set.
char_rom_out's jump.
gd_char_rom_in's jump.
kernal_in's jump.
kernal_out's jump.
all_ram_view's way back: sets bits 1 and 2 of the processor port again.
all_ram_view's jump.
square_info's jump.
clear_view's jump.
step_forward's jump.
show_view's jump.
square_index's jump.
read_object's jump.
The party's square across, 0-15 (west to east).
The party's square down, 0-15 (north to south).
The way the party faces: 0 north, 1 east, 2 south, 3 west (step_forward's table at $C419).
The wall on the side the party faces (square_info); during draw_view, the number of the wall piece being drawn.
The square's byte from the map's third page (square_info): the map at $0600 + the square's number.

Not zero when the view shows objects as sprites (view_init sets up sprites 2-7, draw_view calls draw_objects). The adventure module sets it to 0 ($156B) and keeps the doors' bits in the map's fourth page instead, so in the adventure module's snapshots the object records are never used.
An object record's first byte (read_object $C680, write_object $C636); 0 marks an empty record.
An object record's row, the high half of its second byte.
An object record's column, the low half of its second byte.
An object record's third byte, the picture draw_objects shows for it.
An object record's fourth byte.
The number of the object record in hand, 0-63; $FF when find_free_object finds none.
The border colour view_init sets.
The background colour view_init sets.
The first extra colour of multicolour text, for $D022.
The second extra colour of multicolour text, for $D023.
The colours clear_view gives the view's three bands, top to bottom (with $C05C, $C05D): the adventure module sets the first two, the sky's and the horizon's, for each place ($1165, $1168).
clear_view's colour for the middle band.
clear_view's colour for the bottom band.
The characters clear_view fills the three bands with, $C05E-$C060: $40, $41 and $42.
The sprites' first shared colour, for $D025.
The sprites' second shared colour, for $D026; the sixteen bytes after it are not read by GDRIVE01.
The wall beyond the far left of the view, two squares ahead and one to the left, on the side facing the party; draw_view reads it before the main pass.
The same wall two squares ahead and one to the right.
The map's address, low and high ($C076): $0400, where GEO files load.
map_ptr's high byte: $04.
The screen colour address of the view's top left corner, low and high ($C078): $D87B, row 3 column 3. The adventure module sets it ($1570).
view_colour_ptr's high byte: $D8.
The address of the wall characters, low and high ($C07A): $ED50, WALLS00, fifteen wall shapes of 156 bytes.
wall_chars_ptr's high byte: $ED.
The address of the wall colours, low and high ($C07C): $F674, the fifteen shapes' colours after their characters.
wall_colours_ptr's high byte: $F6.
The screen address of the view's top left corner, low and high ($C07E): $CC7B. The adventure module sets it ($1573).
view_screen_ptr's high byte: $CC.
The address of the view's character buffer, low and high ($C080): $EC00, 11 by 11.
view_chars_ptr's high byte: $EC.
The address of the view's colour buffer, low and high ($C082): $EC80.
view_colours_ptr's high byte: $EC.
The source address of a block copy (copy_rom_block, copy_ram_block) and of load_object_sprites, low and high ($C084).
copy_from's high byte.
The destination address of a block copy, low and high ($C086).
copy_to's high byte.
The address of the screen's sprite pointers, low and high ($C088): $CFF8.
sprite_ptrs_ptr's high byte: $CF.
The address where the objects' sprite images go, low and high ($C08A): $D800, the RAM under the I/O area.
obj_images_ptr's high byte: $D8.
The address of the objects' sprite colours, low and high ($C08C): $ED00, two bytes for each picture.
obj_colours_ptr's high byte: $ED.
The screen height at which view_init puts sprites 2-7.
The across positions of sprites 2 and 3 (and $C08F for 4 and 5, $C090 for 6 and 7).
The across position of sprites 4 and 5.
The across position of sprites 6 and 7.
The high bits of the sprites' across positions, for $D010.
The character a wall shape leaves see-through: 0.
A count, low byte: rows left to fill in clear_view, bytes left to copy in a block copy (with $C094).
A block copy's count, high byte.
The heights in bytes of clear_view's three bands: 55, 11 and 55.
The sprite pointer of the objects' first picture, $60: picture n shows from pointer $60 + n.
The picture shown in each of the eight sprites ($FF for none), filled by draw_objects for sprites 2-7.

Sets up the screen for the view: VIC bank 3, screen $CC00 and characters $D000, multicolour text, the border, background and extra colours ($C057-$C05A). When objects are shown ($C050), also the sprites' shared colours and the positions of sprites 2-7, and clears their priority and width bits.
Keeps Y for view_init: stored here at $C0EE and loaded back by the LDY at $C132 before it returns.

Interrupts off, and the character ROM at $D000: clears bit 2 of the processor port. Each of these switches keeps A by writing it into the LDA that ends it. $C142 char_rom_out sets the bit again and allows interrupts.
Keeps A for gd_char_rom_in: stored here at $C135 and loaded back by the LDA at $C13F before it returns.
Sets bit 2 of the processor port again, putting the I/O chips back over the character ROM, and allows interrupts; keeps A.
Keeps A for char_rom_out: stored here at $C142 and loaded back by the LDA at $C14C before it returns.

Interrupts off and bit 1 of the processor port cleared: the KERNAL ROM's bit. With the port at $37, as gdrive_call ($4078) leaves it, that gives $35, RAM at $E000 where the walls and buffers are and the I/O chips still in; from $36 it gives $34, RAM everywhere. $C15C kernal_in sets it again and allows interrupts.
Keeps A for kernal_out: stored here at $C14F and loaded back by the LDA at $C159 before it returns.
Sets bit 1 of the processor port again, the KERNAL ROM's, and allows interrupts; keeps A.
Keeps A for kernal_in: stored here at $C15C and loaded back by the LDA at $C166 before it returns.
Interrupts off and bits 1 and 2 of the processor port cleared; $C176 sets them again and allows interrupts.
Keeps A for all_ram_view: stored here at $C169 and loaded back by the LDA at $C173 before it returns.
Sets bits 1 and 2 of the processor port again and allows interrupts; keeps A.
Keeps A for all_ram_out: stored here at $C176 and loaded back by the LDA at $C180 before it returns.

Draws the 3D view for the party's square and facing: clears the buffer (clear_view), notes the two far walls at the edges ($C073, $C074), then for each of 23 wall pieces, from the farthest to the nearest, steps to its square (two ahead to here, two left to two right: the tables at $C215 and $C22C), reads the wall on its side ($C243: 0 the side faced, 1 right, 3 left) and draws it (draw_wall). Then copies the buffer to the screen (show_view), adds the objects when they are shown, and reads the square in front (square_info). The party's position is put back after each step.
In draw_view, the square the next wall piece is on: the value the LDY at $C1F0 takes, written at $C1E7 with the square's number (square_index).
In draw_view, the party's column, kept at $C197 so that the LDA at $C1F5 can put it back in party_x after each wall piece's steps.
In draw_view, the party's row, kept at $C19D so that the LDA at $C1FA can put it back in party_y after each piece.
Keeps Y for draw_view: stored here at $C1ED and loaded back by the LDY at $C1FF before it returns.
For each of the 23 wall pieces, how many squares to the right of the party its square is (negative to the left).
For each wall piece, how many squares behind the party its square is: -2 for the farthest row, -1, then 0.
For each wall piece, which side of its square: 0 the side the party faces, 1 the right, 3 the left.

Moves the position A squares to the party's right (negative to the left), for the facing in X: the coordinate the facing makes across ($C28D, $C292: X for north and south, Y for east and west), negated for south and west, wrapping at 16. $C297 move_back takes X one on, moving A squares behind.
In move_right, the number of squares to move, negated for south and west: the value the LDA at $C280 adds, written at $C26A.
In move_right, the low byte of the address the ADC at $C282 reads: move_right writes A there at $C270 from axis_lo indexed by x.
In move_right, the high byte of the address the ADC at $C282 reads: move_right writes A there at $C279 from axis_hi indexed by x.
In move_right, the low byte of the coordinate the STA at $C287 writes back: party_x or party_y, written at $C273 from axis_lo.
In move_right, the high byte of the coordinate the STA at $C287 writes back, written at $C27C from axis_hi.
Keeps A for move_right: the distance asked for, stored at $C25A and loaded back by the LDA at $C28A before it returns.
The coordinate move_right changes for each facing 0-4: low bytes of $C04B or $C04C, with $C292 the high bytes.
The high bytes of the coordinate move_right changes for each facing (axis_lo, $C28D).
Moves the position A squares behind the party (negative ahead): move_right with the facing turned one step on.
Returns the square's number on the map, its row times 16 plus its column, with both kept to 0-15.

Copies the view's 11 by 11 buffer to the screen: characters from $EC00 to the screen at $C07D, colours from $EC80 to colour RAM at $C077, row by row (40 bytes apart), with the KERNAL ROM out so that the buffers under it show.
In show_view, the low byte of the address the LDA at $C2EC reads: show_view writes A there at $C2BB from view_chars_ptr.
In show_view, the high byte of the address the LDA at $C2EC reads: show_view writes A there at $C2C1 from the high byte at $C080.
In show_view, the low byte of the screen address the STA at $C2EF writes characters to: view_screen_ptr at the start ($C2D3), 40 more for each row ($C304).
In show_view, the high byte of the address the STA at $C2EF writes to: show_view writes A there at $C2D9 from the high byte at $C07E; steps it on at $C309.
In show_view, the low byte of the address the LDA at $C2F2 reads: show_view writes A there at $C2C7 from view_colours_ptr.
In show_view, the high byte of the address the LDA at $C2F2 reads: show_view writes A there at $C2CD from the high byte at $C082.
In show_view, the low byte of the colour RAM address the STA at $C2F5 writes to: view_colour_ptr at the start ($C2DF), 40 more for each row ($C312).
In show_view, the high byte of the address the STA at $C2F5 writes to: show_view writes A there at $C2E5 from the high byte at $C078; steps it on at $C317.

Fills the view buffer with its three bands, top to bottom: the heights at $C095 (55, 11 and 55 bytes), the characters at $C05E and colours at $C05B: the sky, the horizon and the ground before the walls are drawn over them. Keeps A, X and Y.
In clear_view, where the LDY at $C362 starts the next band in the buffers: 0 for the first band ($C348), then where the last one ended ($C372).
In clear_view, the character the band is filled with, which the LDA at $C364 takes: written at $C357 from band_chars.
In clear_view, the low byte of the address the STA at $C366 writes to: clear_view writes A there at $C33D from view_chars_ptr.
In clear_view, the high byte of the address the STA at $C366 writes to: clear_view writes A there at $C343 from the high byte at $C080.
In clear_view, the band's colour, which the LDA at $C369 takes: written at $C351 from band_colours.
In clear_view, the low byte of the address the STA at $C36B writes to: clear_view writes A there at $C331 from view_colours_ptr.
In clear_view, the high byte of the address the STA at $C36B writes to: clear_view writes A there at $C337 from the high byte at $C082.
Keeps A for clear_view: stored here at $C322 and loaded back by the LDA at $C37B before it returns.
Keeps X for clear_view: stored here at $C325 and loaded back by the LDX at $C37D before it returns.
Keeps Y for clear_view: stored here at $C328 and loaded back by the LDY at $C37F before it returns.
Reads the wall on side A (from the facing in X) of square Y and draws it (draw_wall) unless it is open (0). Returns with X 3 and Y $40.
Keeps X for wall_piece: stored here at $C385 and loaded back by the LDX at $C395 before it returns.
Keeps Y for wall_piece: stored here at $C388 and loaded back by the LDY at $C397 before it returns.

Returns the wall on side A of square Y, turned by the facing in X: a four-bit number, 0 for open. North and east are the high and low halves of the map's first page ($0400 + the square), south and west those of its second ($0500).
In wall_at, the facing the ADC at $C3B0 adds to the side asked for: written at $C3A0 from X.
In wall_at, the low byte of the address the LDA at $C3BC reads: wall_at writes X there at $C3A6 from map_ptr.
In wall_at, the high byte of the map page the LDA at $C3BC reads: map_ptr's, written at $C3AC, and one more for south and west ($C3B9).
Keeps X for wall_at: stored here at $C39D and loaded back by the LDX at $C3CD before it returns.
Keeps Y for wall_at: stored here at $C39A and loaded back by the LDY at $C3CF before it returns.
Reads the party's square: the wall on the side faced into $C04E (returned in A) and the square's byte on the map's third page ($0600) into $C04F.
In square_info, the low byte of the address the LDA at $C3F0 reads: square_info writes A there at $C3E4 from map_ptr.
In square_info, the high byte of the map page the LDA at $C3F0 reads: two pages on from map_ptr's, written at $C3ED.
Moves the party one square the way it faces, wrapping at the edges of the 16 by 16 map: across by $C419, down by $C41D.
The change across for each facing: 0, +1, 0, -1; $C41D the change down: -1, 0, +1, 0.
The change down for each facing: -1, 0, +1, 0.
Copies 2048 bytes from $C083 to $C085 with the character ROM showing ($C093/$C094 the count). Nothing calls it by its address in any snapshot.
Copies 4681 bytes ($1249) from $C083 to $C085 with the KERNAL ROM out.
The copy itself: bytes from the address at $C083 to the address at $C085, both written into the loop's LDA and STA, until the count in $C093/$C094 runs out.
In copy_block, the low byte of the address the LDA at $C461 reads: copy_block writes A there at $C458 from copy_from; steps it on at $C467.
In copy_block, the high byte of the address the LDA at $C461 reads: copy_block writes A there at $C45E from the high byte at $C084; steps it on at $C46C.
In copy_block, the low byte of the address the STA at $C464 writes to: copy_block writes A there at $C44C from copy_to; steps it on at $C46F.
In copy_block, the high byte of the address the STA at $C464 writes to: copy_block writes A there at $C452 from the high byte at $C086; steps it on at $C474.

Draws wall shape A (1-15) as wall piece $C04E into the view buffer, with the KERNAL ROM out: the shape's characters start 156 bytes times A-1 from $C079 and its colours as far from $C07B; the piece's place in the shape ($C59D), its first column ($C5B4), widths ($C5CB), rows ($C5E2) and steps ($C586) give the rectangle copied. Character 0 is see-through (draw_cell).
In draw_wall, the low byte of the wall shape's offset (156 times its number less one), which the LDA at $C4AE takes to add to wall_colours_ptr: written at $C49D.
In draw_wall, the piece's place in the shape (piece_offset), which the LDA at $C4D6 takes to add to view_colours_ptr: written at $C4C4.
In draw_wall, the column the LDY at $C4FE starts each row at (piece_step), written at $C4F2.
In draw_wall, the cells left in the row: the LDA at $C50C takes it, set to the piece's width at $C4FB and to 2 at $C512, counted down at $C509.
In draw_wall, the piece's width (piece_width) for each row after the first, which the LDA at $C510 takes: written at $C4F8.
In draw_wall, the rows left to draw: the LDA at $C534 takes it, set to piece_rows at $C4EC and counted down at $C531.

Copies one character and its colour of the wall shape into the buffer at column Y unless it is the see-through 0; at the piece's edges (X below 2) also draws the neighbouring cells, and in the middle column takes the far edge walls ($C073, $C074) into account.
In draw_cell, the low byte of the wall shape's characters the LDA at $C53C reads: wall_chars_ptr plus the shape's offset, written by draw_wall at $C4A3.
In draw_cell, the high byte of the wall shape's characters, written by draw_wall at $C4AA.
In draw_cell, the low byte of the buffer row the STA at $C544 writes characters to: view_chars_ptr plus the piece's place, written by draw_wall at $C4CA and 11 more for each row ($C51B).
In draw_cell, the high byte of the character buffer row, written by draw_wall at $C4D2 and carried at $C520.
In draw_cell, the low byte of the wall shape's colours the LDA at $C547 reads: wall_colours_ptr plus the shape's offset, written by draw_wall at $C4B3.
In draw_cell, the high byte of the wall shape's colours, written by draw_wall at $C4BA.
In draw_cell, the low byte of the buffer row the STA at $C54A writes colours to: view_colours_ptr plus the piece's place, written by draw_wall at $C4DB and 11 more for each row ($C529).
In draw_cell, the high byte of the colour buffer row, written by draw_wall at $C4E3 and carried at $C52E.
Keeps X for draw_cell, written at $C551; the LDX at $C56C sets X to 1 instead on the paths that drew an edge.
For each of the 23 wall pieces, a step draw_wall uses between rows.
For each wall piece, where its characters start in a wall shape's 156 bytes.
For each wall piece, its first column in the 11-wide buffer.
For each wall piece, its width count.
For each wall piece, its number of rows.
Clears all 64 object records (the map's fourth page, $0700). The adventure module never calls it: in its maps that page holds the doors' bits, two for each side of each square (door_state, $1143).
Finds the first empty object record (first byte 0), stores its number in $C056 and writes the record in hand ($C051-$C055) there; $C056 is $FF when all 64 are used.
In find_free_object, the free record's offset (four times its number), which the ADC at $C61E adds to the records' address: written at $C618 from Y.
Writes the record in hand into record $C056: the first byte ($C051), the row and column as one byte ($C052 high, $C053 low), $C054 and $C055.
In write_object, the column, which the ORA at $C64F joins to the row in the record's second byte: written at $C645.
write_object for the record $C056.
Points $FB/$FC at object record A: the map's fourth page plus four times A.
Keeps A for object_address: the record number, stored at $C66B and loaded back by the LDA at $C67D before it returns.
Reads record $C056 into $C051-$C055 (the second byte split into row and column).
Keeps A for read_object: stored here at $C680 and loaded back by the LDA at $C6B3 before it returns.
Keeps Y for read_object: stored here at $C683 and loaded back by the LDY at $C6B5 before it returns.
Keeps X for read_object: stored here at $C686 and loaded back by the LDX at $C6B7 before it returns.

Shows the objects the party can see as sprites 2-7: walks the squares ahead in six lines of sight ($C82D their starts in the tables at $C7E8, $C7FF and $C816), stopping each at a wall, and gives the pictures of the objects there (object_pictures, $C861) to the line's pair of sprites ($C833). Sets their pointers ($C098 plus the picture), colours and multicolour bits from the colour table ($C08B), turns them on, then reads the record of any object on the party's own square (object_here).
In draw_objects, the line of sight being walked, 0-5: the LDX at $C6FC takes it, 0 at the start ($C6F6), one more for each line ($C73A).
In draw_objects, the step of the line in hand, written at $C719 so the LDY at $C726 can take it up again.
In draw_objects, the party's column, kept at $C6EB so that the LDA at $C72C can put it back in party_x after each step of a line.
In draw_objects, the party's row, kept at $C6F1 so that the LDA at $C731 can put it back in party_y.
In draw_objects, whether the line stops: the LDA at $C736 takes the wall just read ($C729) or 1 after objects were found ($C7E2), and the line goes on only on 0.
In draw_objects, the low byte of the address the STA at $C762 writes to: draw_objects writes A there at $C6C9 from sprite_ptrs_ptr.
In draw_objects, the high byte of the address the STA at $C762 writes to: draw_objects writes A there at $C6CF from the high byte at $C088.
In draw_objects, the low byte of the address the LDA at $C76A reads: draw_objects writes A there at $C6D5 from obj_colours_ptr.
In draw_objects, the high byte of the address the LDA at $C76A reads: draw_objects writes A there at $C6DB from the high byte at $C08C.
In draw_objects, the multicolour bits for the sprites, built at $C770 and joined by the ORA at $C780 into $D01C: written as 0 at $C749.
In draw_objects, the bits of the sprites to show, built at $C766 and joined by the ORA at $C78A into $D015: written as 0 at $C746.
Keeps X for draw_objects: stored here at $C6BD and loaded back by the LDX at $C795 before it returns.
Keeps Y for draw_objects: stored here at $C6C0 and loaded back by the LDY at $C797 before it returns.
Keeps A for draw_objects: stored here at $C6BA and loaded back by the LDA at $C799 before it returns.
draw_objects for a square of the line: the objects there (object_pictures) fill the line's two sprites, the nearer first.
In draw_objects, the first object's picture (object_pictures), which the LDA at $C7C8 takes: written at $C7A4.
In draw_objects, the line's offset into the pictures, which the ADC at $C7CE adds: written at $C79E.
In draw_objects, the second picture for the line's second sprite: the LDA at $C7D4 takes it, the second object's picture from Y ($C7A7) or the first's ($C7C2).
For each step of draw_objects' lines of sight, the squares across from the party.
For each step of the lines of sight, the squares behind (negative ahead).
For each step of the lines of sight, the wall side to test (stop at a wall), or negative to look for objects on the square.
Where each of the six lines of sight starts in the tables at $C7E8.
For each of the six lines of sight, the first of its pair of sprites: 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6.
Finds the object record on the party's square, if any, and reads it (read_object) with its number in $C056.
In object_here, the party's square (square_index), the value the LDA at $C851 compares with each record's second byte: written at $C83C.
The pictures of up to two objects on the square: the first in A, the second in Y ($FF where none).
In object_pictures, the square looked at (square_index), which the CMP at $C87D tests each record's second byte against: written at $C86C.
In object_pictures, the Y it returns when no second object is found: $FF, written at $C863.
In object_pictures, the first object's picture, $FF until one is found: the LDA at $C898 returns it, written at $C866 and $C88B.

Copies object $C056's two sprite images (128 bytes from $C083) to its place at $C089 (128 bytes each) with all RAM showing, and the last byte of each image, its colour, into the colour table at $C08B. Nothing calls it by its address in any snapshot.
In load_object_sprites, the low byte of the address the LDA at $C8ED reads: load_object_sprites writes A there at $C8D6 from copy_from.
In load_object_sprites, the high byte of the address the LDA at $C8ED reads: load_object_sprites writes A there at $C8DC from the high byte at $C084.
In load_object_sprites, the low byte of where the STA at $C8F0 writes the images: obj_images_ptr plus 128 times the object's number, written at $C8C7.
In load_object_sprites, the high byte of where the images go: 0 at $C8AF, built up by the shifts at $C8BD, then obj_images_ptr's high byte added at $C8D0.
In load_object_sprites, the low byte of the address the STA at $C8FE writes to: load_object_sprites writes A there at $C8E2 from obj_colours_ptr.
In load_object_sprites, the high byte of the address the STA at $C8FE writes to: load_object_sprites writes A there at $C8E8 from the high byte at $C08C.
Keeps A for load_object_sprites: stored here at $C8A1 and loaded back by the LDA at $C908 before it returns.
Keeps Y for load_object_sprites: stored here at $C8A4 and loaded back by the LDY at $C90A before it returns.
Keeps X for load_object_sprites: stored here at $C8A7 and loaded back by the LDX at $C90C before it returns.
The 241 bytes after the last routine, which GDRIVE01 carries on every side: $FF $91 and $00 $6E over and over, read by nothing. The jump table's three last entries point at their first byte.
